title: Chevron preparing ~$1B sale package of stakes in older U.S. Gulf plays - TradingView
content: Chevron CVX is exploring the sale of some of its older oil and gas assets in the U.S. Gulf, as it seeks to focus on newer projects and high-growth opportunities in the region, Reuters reported Wednesday. "We are initiating ​the process of marketing some of our mature Gulf of America producing assets, including ⁠Petronius, Tubular Bells, and Llano, as well as working interest in several other operated and non-operated fields," a company ​spokesperson told Reuters. The sales reportedly are expected to raise ~$1B, with interest expected from international operators that specialize in offshore development and ​that are seeking to grow their U.S. Gulf footprint, as well as U.S. companies ​focused on the ⁠basin. Chevron CVX operates the Petronius asset with Talos Energy, owns 100% of Tubular Bells after initially holding 43% but assuming the rest ⁠following its ​takeover of Hess, and inherited its 50% position in Shell-operated Llano from Hess. Retail investors in Sellas Life Sciences (SLS) are floating multibillion-dollar buyout scenarios and steep share-price gains after CEO Angelos Stergiou marked the company’s 15th anniversary with a post about its “next chapter.” SLS stock jumped 5% on Monday to $10.49, snapping three straight losing sessions. In his LinkedIn post, Stergiou reflected on Sellas’ growth from a private startup into a public biotech advancing investigational cancer treatments GPS and SLS009. “Reaching 15 years isn't just about celebrating our history; it is about stepping into our next chapter with even greater focus, drive, and resolve,” he said. He acknowledged past setbacks and thanked shareholders, employees and trial participants, while reaffirming the company’s commitment to patients. “Our mission remains deeply personal, and our promise to the patients we aim to serve is steadfast. We look forward, God willing, to the best chapters that are still to be written with GPS and SLS009,” he added. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment for SLS slipped to ‘bearish’ from ‘bullish’ levels a day ago amid a 258% jump in 24-hour message volumes. One user said: “My opinion, Dr. Stergiou’s message was a master-class at reassuring EVERYONE that all is well.” A user also floated a minimum $40 billion valuation. Another user argued for a $50 billion valuation, calling a $247-per-share figure. A separate user proposed a $120 billion buyout scenario and also predicted a share price of $540-plus. Across bullish share-price predictions, including scenarios tied to clinical results, targets ranged from $100 to over $540. Discussing buyout news in case of favorable data, one user said: “If BO news post good data then there’s no stopping this beast (really no explanation required as it could go full berserker mode).” BO means buyout. Another user challenged the lofty valuations and said: “I will be so glad to get out of this ticker when it hits $15 again.” The CEO’s message comes as investors have been searching for potential deal signals in recent months. In June, a filing disclosed changes to executive severance arrangements, including lump-sum payment provisions for Stergiou. For CFO John Burns and chief development officer Dragan Cicic, qualifying departures within one month before or one year after a change of control would trigger 15 months of salary, the annual target bonus, up to 18 months of health-coverage reimbursements and full vesting of unvested equity. Sellas’ conference plans have provided another talking point. The company is listed at Booth 138, with a 20-by-30-foot space, for the Dec.12- Dec.15 American Society of Hematology (ASH) meeting in New Orleans. Major exhibitors include Eli Lilly, Pfizer, Merck, AbbVie and Bristol Myers Squibb. The booth size has fueled speculation about a partnership or acquisition. Currently, investors are awaiting data from Sellas’ two lead programs. The Phase 3 Regal trial is testing GPS, an immunotherapy targeting WT1, in acute myeloid leukemia (AML) patients who achieved a second complete remission following salvage treatment. Its final-analysis process is triggered by 80 deaths. Sellas reported 78 events as of May 11. Reaching 80 precedes database lock, data review and analysis before results are disclosed. The company also expects fourth-quarter topline data from its 80-patient Phase 2 SLS009 study in newly diagnosed AML, including patients with early resistance to azacitidine and venetoclax. SLS009 is also being explored in pancreatic cancer. Preclinical findings from last month showed 17.9% apoptosis (programmed cell death) in a patient-derived tumor model resistant to Daraxonrasib, versus 2.8% with Daraxonrasib alone. (AVGO) reversed overnight losses to edge up 0.3% late Monday as a 10-year cloud agreement with NTT Docomo did little to ease retail skepticism, with traders seeking a recovery catalyst after CEO Hock Tan’s AI “casino” remarks. AVGO stock rose nearly 2% on Monday to close at $334.59, snapping three straight sessions of losses. Broadcom extended its 2019 deal with Docomo, in which the companies will align their long-term tech roadmaps to advance the private cloud underpinning the Japanese telecom operator’s digital services. The company called it Broadcom Japan’s first “comprehensive” 10-year agreement covering VMware software licenses, technical assistance and maintenance support. Financial terms were not disclosed. VMware Cloud Foundation will be at the core of the infrastructure. The deal targets three priorities: keeping services available during system upgrades, strengthening security and resilience, and accelerating the delivery of new services. Docomo will use the platform to expand capacity and manage traffic spikes, improve security patching and anomaly detection, and run virtual machines and containers on a common platform. Automation across development, testing and releases will help shorten the time needed to introduce new features. The companies also plan to expand AI-driven operations and prepare the infrastructure for future developments, including 6G and IOWN. The agreement comes a week after Tan’s comments at a Singapore panel, where he called capital the biggest constraint on further AI development as Broadcom works through wafer and memory shortages. “A lot of investors have no clue what they're investing in, but set very extreme expectations, only to find out that it's almost like they are in a casino gambling,” Tan said when asked about cheaper AI models, Reuters noted. His remarks addressed investment into the broader AI sector. Tan also acknowledged that Anthropic and OpenAI had shown an ability to generate significant revenue from their latest models deployed for AI personal assistants. SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk also subsequently responded, saying, “No crying in the casino,” weighing in on Tan’s concerns about speculative AI investments. The asset manager’s ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK) bought 102,280 CRWV shares on Monday for $6.3 million, according to its website. The firm also bought 30,218 shares of CRWV for $1.8 million through the ARK Next Generation Technology ETF (ARKW). The purchase comes as Wall Street and Main Street remain concerned about the company’s ballooning debt levels. CoreWeave reported $35.6 billion in total debt as of June 30, while its second-quarter net interest expense rose to $640 million from $267 million a year earlier. Research and advisory firm Gartner recently said in a report that artificial intelligence infrastructure investments are in danger as concerns over bloated AI capex mount. The firm said that as the commercial duopoly for primary frontier models consolidates around Anthropic and OpenAI, the cash flows to meet that massive computing asset base from neoclouds are not scaling proportionally with upfront costs. Meanwhile, major Wall Street analysts are also taking opposing stances on CoreWeave. MoffettNathanson and BNP Paribas lowered their price targets on CoreWeave, while Goldman Sachs took a more positive outlook. MoffettNathanson slashed CRWV stock’s target to $89 from $107 and kept a ‘Neutral’ rating on the shares, citing its “staggering financial obligations.” BNP Paribas also cut its price target on CoreWeave to $117 from $169 and maintained an ‘Outperform’ rating, according to The Fly. The firm said that it sees a continued deterioration in investor confidence amid its debt obligations. While higher financing costs could contain the company's ability to fund future growth, the shares are "seemingly discounting some liquidity concerns," the analyst reportedly said in a research note. However, Goldman Sachs upgraded the stock to ‘Buy’ from ‘Neutral’ and set a price target of $106, implying upside of more than 73% from its last close. The firm said ongoing volatility in the credit market raises questions about whether CoreWeave can finance its next phase of growth, and at what pace. However, Goldman also said the ongoing debate over demand for frontier vs. off-frontier intelligence, and CoreWeave's annual recurring revenue per megawatt and unlevered internal rate of return, are "biased to the upside" over the next 24 months because of tight supply. The analyst also said that CoreWeave is differentiated from other neoclouds. Last week, Dan Ives, Yorkville Ives partner and senior managing director analyst, said in an interview that the recent sell-off was an overreaction, as the broader AI demand story remains intact. “I'm not saying there's not some issues in terms as rates go higher. But given the demand, given backlog, I think this is ultimately a false narrative,” he said, while also highlighting that the sharp drop has created an opportunity for investors. EyePoint Pharmaceuticals (EYPT), CoreWeave (CRWV) and Eos Energy Enterprises (EOSE) hit fresh 52-week lows Monday as a failed drug trial, debt refinancing concerns, and weaker full-year revenue expectations weighed on the stocks. EyePoint stock crashed 85%, while CoreWeave and Eos Energy stocks dropped 0.4% and 0.5%, respectively. EyePoint Pharmaceuticals stock crashed to a record low of $0.4 after the company reported disappointing results from LUCIA, its second pivotal Phase 3 study of DURAVYU, an experimental treatment for wet age-related macular degeneration (AMD). The drug failed to show that it worked as well as aflibercept in protecting vision at Weeks 52 and 56, hurting its chances of approval for the eye condition. The setback prompted the company to lay off 53% of its workforce, with the restructuring expected to bring $30 million in annualized savings and incur about $9 million in severance expenses. EyePoint reported roughly $118 million in cash and equivalents as of Sept. 30 and plans to concentrate its remaining resources on Phase 3 studies of DURAVYU for diabetic macular edema (DME). However, on Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the stock flipped to ‘extremely bullish’ from ‘bearish’. CoreWeave stock fell to a new annual low of $59.25 as analysts cut price targets amid concerns about its debt obligations and reliance on external funding. BNP Paribas lowered its price target to $117 from $169 while retaining an ‘Outperform’ rating. MoffettNathanson cut its target to $89 from $107 and maintained a ‘Neutral’ rating. The analysts highlighted the potential consequences of weaker investor confidence and expensive financing. CoreWeave needs capital to expand its data center infrastructure and support growing demand for computing capacity. Higher borrowing costs and limited access to capital markets could complicate its expansion plans and weigh on shareholder returns. Retail sentiment around the stock remained ‘extremely bullish’. Eos Energy Enterprises stock touched a two-year low of $1.72 despite reporting preliminary third-quarter (Q3) revenue of $82 million to $83 million, a sequential growth of 19% to 21%. However, investors focused on the company’s expectation that 2026 revenue would land in the lower half of its previously announced $300 million to $350 million range. The updated outlook follows an earlier reduction in the company's revenue forecast in August. Eos has recorded eight consecutive quarters of improving gross margins, but its margins remain deeply negative as it works to increase production and improve manufacturing efficiency at its Thorn Hill facility. Retail sentiment around the stock remained ‘bearish’. So far this year, EYPT, CRWV and EOSE stocks have declined between 14% and 97%. With a deep upstream base, a growing Permian footprint and refining and marketing arms, the group sits across much of the energy chain. Crude anchors the energy complex, so a push higher in the barrel tends to feed quickly through the producers that lift it. When oil firms, the output each field delivers fetches a stronger price, lifting the cash a large producer can generate without any change to the volume of barrels it brings to the surface. That leverage is central to the upstream business. The upstream arm finds and produces crude oil and natural gas across a spread of regions, feeding the barrels that anchor the group's earnings. The downstream arm refines that crude into gasoline, diesel, jet fuel and other products, while the marketing arm carries those fuels to end customers through a wide branded network. This integrated design lets the group capture value at several stages of the chain at after. Few threads have shaped the group's recent production as much as its position in the Permian basin, the vast shale region straddling the American Southwest that has become the engine of domestic oil growth. A large and contiguous acreage base there feeds a steady, growing stream of barrels that the group can scale with relative speed. The group's Permian holdings carry a mix of owned and royalty acreage that trims the cost of each barrel, a feature prized when crude firms. Readers following Oil and Gas Stocks can place this update within its wider category. Beyond the Permian, the group runs a spread of operations across several continents, from deepwater fields and gas developments to long-life ventures in established oil regions. Large natural gas developments, including sizable liquefied natural gas ventures, add a thread tied to the growing global trade in gas. Those projects lengthen the group's production base and tie it to demand across many markets, broadening the mix beyond crude alone. The downstream arm turns crude into the fuels that move the economy, and its earnings swing with the margin between the cost of crude and the price of refined products. A wide refining margin can lift the arm even when the barrel is quieter, giving the group a thread that moves on its own rhythm distinct from the oil price. Large, complex refineries can process a range of crude grades, letting the group lean toward cheaper feedstock when spreads favor it. A defining feature of the larger energy groups is dependable cash generation across the cycle, and the market often reads the majors through that lens. When crude firms, the gap between the oil price and the cost of lifting each barrel widens, feeding the cash a producer can direct toward drilling, debt reduction and distributions to holders. The group has long carried a reputation for steady cash distributions to the holders of its stock, a feature that keeps it a staple of many broad market baskets. Alongside its core oil and gas base, the group has leaned into lower-carbon threads, from renewable fuels and hydrogen to carbon capture and storage ventures. These efforts sit beside the barrels that anchor earnings, pointing the group toward a wider set of markets over the coming arc of the energy landscape. The group has built and acquired ventures in renewable diesel and related fuels, tying part of the business to the shift toward lower-emission transport. The bank identified commodity prices, refining margins, and operational execution as key risks to its outlook. Piper Sandler has a target of $243. MarketBeat's data lists an average 12-month price target of $213.42 across 28 analysts, with a high of $243 and a low of $90. Our strong second quarter performance is a result of disciplined investment and strong execution that drove record U.S. upstream production, record crude throughput in our U.S. refineries, and exceptional reliability across key assets." After a steep climb driven by worry that global supply might tighten, the benchmark drifted lower as those fears eased and traders weighed the barrels flowing into the market. For a producer of this scale, softer crude trims the cash each barrel brings in, yet the effect is rarely uniform across the business. As crude eased, refining margins stayed firm, a detail that carried weight for the downstream arm. Refining spreads capture the gap between the cost of crude fed into a plant and the value of the fuels that emerge. When those spreads stay healthy even as crude softens, the refining side can lean into the difference. The company runs a meaningful refining and marketing operation, with plants able to process a range of crude grades and to tilt output toward the fuels in strongest demand. Firm margins there help steady group earnings when crude prices wobble. Exploration and production pull crude and natural gas from fields around the world. Refining and marketing turn those barrels into gasoline, diesel and jet fuel. A chemicals arm converts hydrocarbons into the materials behind plastics and packaging. title: Why Did XOM, CVX, MPC Stocks Surge To 52-Week Highs Today? - TradingView
content: Shares of energy companies Exxon Mobil Corp. (XOM), Chevron Corp. (CVX), and Marathon Petroleum Corp. (MPC) surged to annual highs on Monday as oil prices rallied amid growing geopolitical tensions. Brent crude prices touched nearly $110 a barrel on Monday as tensions in the Middle East continued to ratchet up. A series of recent escalations, including attacks on commercial ships near the Strait of Hormuz, Houthi missile strikes on Saudi Arabia, and Ukraine’s strike on a Russian refinery, stoked fears about a further constraint in fuel supplies, sending prices higher. Worries continued despite the U.S. government’s efforts to curtail rising prices, including planned fuel releases and changes to U.S. sanctions on Russian imported fuel. Since the U.S.-Iran war began in February, energy prices have been climbing steadily, boosting energy companies. As per Koyfin data, energy stocks have outperformed the S&P 500 by a significant margin in 2026. Exxon Mobil, Chevron, and Marathon Petroleum shares surged to 52-week highs on Monday before closing lower amid the steep climb in oil prices. XOM stock hit an annual high of $179.30 during trading hours on Monday before closing about 0.4% down. CVX stock surged to a 52-week high of $225.67, but ended the session 0.28% lower. MPC stock rallied to a 52-week high of $493.98 during regular trading, but finished the day nearly 1% down. Retail sentiment around XOM, CVX and MPC stocks was ‘bullish’ at the time of writing on Stocktwits. title: Better Oil Stock: Chevron (CVX) vs. ExxonMobil (XOM) - The Motley Fool
content: Which of these integrated energy giants is a better investment right now? Chevron (CVX +0.47%) and ExxonMobil (XOM +0.13%) are two of the world's largest integrated energy companies. They both own upstream exploration and extraction businesses, midstream pipelines, and downstream refineries. Over the past 12 months, Chevron's stock has rallied 45% while ExxonMobil's stock has risen 58%. Both stocks benefited from rising oil prices, but which stock is the better buy right now? Chevron is smaller than ExxonMobil, but both companies generate most of their revenue from their upstream businesses. However, Chevron generates more of its profits (about 80%) from its upstream business than ExxonMobil (about 70%). That's because ExxonMobil operates a larger downstream business -- which acts as a secondary profit engine -- than Chevron. ExxonMobil's downstream business produces a lot of petrochemicals, while Chevron's downstream business has minimal exposure to that market. When crude oil prices rise, upstream businesses typically grow their revenues faster than their expenses. However, downstream businesses often struggle as their input costs rise. When crude oil prices decline, upstream businesses struggle, but downstream businesses fare better -- as long as the crack spread (between crude oil costs and retail fuel prices) remains stable. Therefore, Chevron's streamlined, upstream-heavy business model makes it a more attractive investment than ExxonMobil when oil prices spike. But when oil prices pull back, ExxonMobil's scale and downstream diversification could make it a more compelling investment. Missed Nvidia in 2009? But from 2025 to 2028, analysts expect its EPS to grow at a 20% CAGR as it integrates its recent acquisition of Pioneer Natural Resources (which expanded its reach in the Permian Basin), increases its production in Guyana, and prioritizes the production of higher-margin chemical performance products and specialized fuels at its downstream business. Its stock also trades at 15 times next year's earnings. Chevron and ExxonMobil both look fundamentally cheap because they're valued as cyclical commodity stocks rather than higher-growth energy plays. However, they're both still solid long-term investments for investors who can stomach the short-term fluctuations in oil prices. But if I could only pick one, I'd choose Chevron over ExxonMobil for three simple reasons: it has more exposure to rising oil prices, it's growing faster, and it pays a higher dividend. title: Is Chevron Stock Worth More Than Its Competitors? - Trefis
content: Chevron (CVX) stock currently trades at 21.5 times earnings, giving it the second-highest P/E among a peer group of six oil and gas companies. Yet the stock recorded the smallest gain in that group after rising 53.7% over the year to October 16, 2026. Three refiners in the same peer group saw their shares more than double during that period. So what does Chevron deliver for a price near the top of its group? Across the four fiscal quarters that ended June 30, 2026, Chevron outperformed Exxon Mobil, the only other integrated oil and gas company in the group. Chevron reported revenue growth of 11.2%, compared to 9.6% at Exxon Mobil. The company also kept 12.4% of its sales as operating profit, whereas its rival retained 10.7%. Despite trailing in these metrics, Exxon Mobil commands a higher valuation at 22.8 times earnings. Comparisons with the rest of the peer group depend on the underlying business. The operators that refine and sell fuel include Marathon Petroleum, Phillips 66 and Valero Energy. All three grew faster than Chevron and trade at lower P/Es, yet none kept more than 7.5% of its sales as operating profit. ConocoPhillips, an exploration and production company, earned the widest margin in the group at 21.9%. It trades at a lower P/E than Chevron while growing more slowly. When measured against its single direct competitor running the same integrated business model, Chevron delivers stronger results for slightly less money. The timing of Chevron’s operating profit reveals a heavy tilt toward the final period. Out of a total $25.8 billion generated over those four quarters, $14.3 billion arrived in the single quarter that ended June 30, 2026. Chevron recorded an operating margin of 21% in that specific period, up from 9.1% a year earlier. Across each of the three preceding quarters, that margin stayed below 9%. Chevron operates two primary segments. Its Upstream segment produces the oil and gas, while its Downstream segment refines and sells fuel. During a July 31, 2026 call, management said adjusted earnings from producing oil and gas rose on higher prices, higher volumes and favorable timing effects. In the refining business, management stated that adjusted earnings rose mainly on higher refining margins and favorable timing effects. Chevron has also lowered its costs. Management said the company cut $3 billion of costs over the twelve months before the call, ahead of schedule. Management’s targets for 2030 project steady growth. These targets are set at flat oil and gas prices, which sit below those recorded at the time of its July call. On the July 31, 2026 call, management said it still expects Chevron’s production to grow 2% to 3% a year. The company also expects adjusted free cash flow, its own measure of cash left after investment, to grow by more than 10% a year on average. The market currently values Chevron at a P/E near the top of its group, a multiple measured on four quarters of earnings that include the June quarter. So far, the June quarter stands as the only recent period in which Chevron earned a margin that wide. Operating margin remains the key metric to watch in the company’s next report, expected on or around October 30, 2026. Not necessarily on Chevron alone, if your goal is long-term wealth.
